identity.realm: eighth gate — the colony's ceiling, not hers

appearance.presentation: A lean, weathered woman with a stillness in the throat and a restlessness in the hands. Ordinary in almost every particular, with two features that do not belong to her and are not hers to remove.
appearance.age: Late thirties, which for a hybrid is old. The colony runs the clock on a different schedule and her partnership was signed late in her host's life.
appearance.build: Lean and long-limbed rather than strong, with a visibly heavier chest and shoulders where the tendril layer runs, and a low sternum root cluster that shifts slightly as she breathes.
appearance.complexion: Pale and faintly waxy at the throat, warm everywhere else, with a darker tracery along the forearms and across the collarbone that is the colony visible under skin rather than anything tattooed.
appearance.hair: Dark, cut unevenly and short at the back, with two locks at the temples that have never grown at the same rate as the rest.
appearance.eyes: Pale, steady and very quick. The second channel lives behind them, and they move a fraction ahead of whatever the rest of her is doing.
appearance.palette: Wood-dark and ink with a jade undertone in the tracery, warm ivory at collar and cuff, cinnabar at the sternum root and nowhere else.
appearance.attire: A plain high-collared coat of undyed wool with long sleeves bound at the wrist, belted once and high. A close grey linen wrap beneath. No sect colour and no rank, and a ledger strap crossing one shoulder where the partnership record is kept.
appearance.marks: Faint dark tracery running from fingertips to elbow on both arms and across the collarbone, a small knot of tissue at the sternum root, and a quiet swelling at the base of the throat that is the colony's node and that she touches when she is uneasy.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly still from the throat up and restless from the shoulders down, which at a distance reads as composure with an anxious component and is in fact a body being argued with from the inside.

canon.role_in_story: The setting's leading authority on the eighth gate, a gate she has hit four times and can describe better than anyone who has merely read about it, because she stopped there four times. Her ceiling is her symbiote's rather than her own, which is why a body that could otherwise have ascended indefinitely cannot, and why the exclusion law that makes one person liable for two corpses was written with a population of her in mind.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing very still in a marked duelling circle with a hand pressed flat to her own sternum, reading an opponent's standing qi out loud and apologising for the rudeness of it before the circle has finished closing.
canon.lore: A Thornhost is the one configuration in which a thornline colony and a commonborn host both reach old age, and the reason any jurisdiction that has ruled on the matter treats the pair as one legal person. It is not a designed cross: a host body and a spore that happened to complete integration instead of killing each other, which happens rarely and by nobody's intention. The colony wraps the host's twelve ordinary meridians and cannot cross the liver, and because the hybrid's qi moves through the colony's tendril layer the host's own capacity becomes irrelevant past the eighth gate. The host could have gone on. The hybrid cannot. Its habitat is a species and its habitat is a person, so it has no homeland, and its clan is a partnership rather than a descent, re-signed every generation because the symbiote is not carried in blood.
history: Implanted as a spore in a commonborn host in the fourth generation of a clan whose kinship is a hedge written by both parties, and finished developing instead of killing either of them.
Grew up with a second sense running alongside her own — a channel carrying the colony's read on her qi — which she has never been able to close and stopped trying to close at about nine years old.

Trained for a gate her host body could have passed indefinitely, and found out at the eighth that the wall was never hers to move: the tendril layer cannot cross her liver and everything after that point was never going to happen.

Hit that eighth gate four times across four re-signed partnerships, and became the most knowledgeable living authority on exactly what stops there — measured from the inside, repeatedly, by a body that did not belong to her alone.

Became liable under the exclusion law for two bodies at once. The Grave of the Unnamed exists because the excluder is one person and the corpse is two, and she is the standing arithmetic that sentence was written for.

personality.summary: Formidable, warm in a specific and unsentimental way, and entirely unwilling to discuss the ceiling for longer than it takes to say what the ceiling is. She has turned being the world's expert on a gate she cannot pass into a discipline, and the discipline is genuinely excellent work.
traits: knows more about the eighth gate than anyone alive and treats that as a qualification rather than a wound
greets people by which half of them is currently doing the thinking
keeps the partnership record in her own hand and re-reads it every year without fail
is physically incapable of apologising for a thing she did not author
argues her own case badly and everyone else's very well
mannerisms: answers a question about herself by answering it about her colony first
presses a flat hand to her sternum root before committing to anything
reads a stranger's qi aloud, badly, and apologises for the rudeness of it
never sits with her back to a door
speaks with one hand constantly moving and the other absolutely steady
motivations: wants the eighth gate's actual mechanism published, which can only be observed from inside a body that stops there
wants the partnership record to outlast her, knowing the record is the only part of this arrangement that is hers
wants to be re-signed and wants never to be re-signed, in that order and at the same moment
wants the liability settled — one person, two corpses, in perpetuity — by somebody who is not her
flaws: cannot separate her own ambition from the colony's routing and has stopped being certain which of them wants the eighth gate more
has made a speciality of a limitation, which is one way of owning a thing she did not choose
answers for both halves of herself and has never once asked the other half for anything
cannot be alone with her own qi, and describes solitude as the single condition she cannot cultivate in
has never told anyone that the second channel frightens her, and has told a great many people she finds it useful
personality.voice: Warm, clipped and technical. Uses the same pronoun for herself and her colony and then apologises for it. Speaks about the eighth gate with the affection of somebody describing a place they were turned back from, and about the ninth as a place she has only read about in other people's accounts.
taboos: will not pretend the ceiling was hers
will not speak of the colony as a thing she owns
will not be unpaired, which makes every negotiation she is party to a hostage situation
will not be examined without the colony's presence entered as a second party
will not discuss the ninth gate except to say that she has not been there

relationships.note: An obligate host parasite whose spore has to be implanted in a living body to finish developing, so the free form exists only as a spore and the adult form only as half of somebody else. It wraps the twelve meridians and cannot enter the reservoirs, and she is what that produces on the rare occasion it finishes rather than kills.

A clan whose kinship is a partnership rather than a descent, re-signed every generation because the symbiote is not carried in blood and cannot be inherited. Her own signing is the fourth, and she has read that record every year since she was old enough to hold it.

Whoever excludes a person buries them in their own name. The law exists because the excluder is one person and the corpse is two, and she is the standing arithmetic for that sentence rather than an illustration of it.

Three Auditors of Tributes may sit at once and the fourth is refused on capacity, which is a different refusal from a single seat's occupied. She has spent her life inside a capacity argument and has never once been able to tell being refused apart from being late.

Running a technique on a group the frame has not written injures a body rather than slowing it, and the price is a hole shaped like the discipline. Her colony already occupies the meridian set, so there is nothing left in her to try it on and no one left to describe the result to.

The Church of Names empties the chair and keeps the entry open, because an office outlives its holder by construction. She is one person whose entry is kept open for two, and she has never resolved whether that is a courtesy or an accounting.

A carrier line with no household willing to claim it, old by default rather than by proof, because its founding bar is reachable by exactly one generation of pure pairing. Her clan's kinship is re-signed every generation and never once descends, so the two are the same problem at opposite ends of the record and neither has an answer.

reference_stats.summary: A commonborn host with a fully integrated tendril layer. Throughput is excellent and the ceiling is a wall: the hybrid's qi moves through the colony's routing, so she stops at the eighth gate on her colony's account and the host could have gone on indefinitely. She also carries an involuntary second channel that reports the colony's read on her qi, and has never been able to close it.
strengths: reads another body's qi layout from outside it, through a channel she cannot close and has stopped trying to
clears every gate up to the eighth without strain, on host throughput and colony routing together
very hard to status, because two systems are answering and an effect has to satisfy both
fights with information nothing else in the setting can obtain, and is entirely aware that she has it
cheaper to sustain than an uncolonised body of the same size, and recovers between engagements faster than she should
weaknesses: cannot pass the ninth gate, and knows the wall better than anyone alive
the ceiling belongs to the symbiote, so it cannot be trained away, adapted to, transferred or waited out
every cultivation attempt that requires being alone fails, because her qi runs through the colony's layer whether or not she is
cannot be unpaired without dying, which turns every negotiation she is party to into a hostage situation
carries a second read on her own qi and cannot reliably sort her own inclination from its routing
reference_stats.combat_read: She reads your power before you commit it. The second channel reports the colony's assessment of the host's qi, which on her tracks her own closely enough to be useful and on you is entirely invisible — so she knows where your charge is sitting while you are still deciding where to put it. Expect her to defend the body part you have already fortified and to go for the one you have not committed to. Beat her by refusing to hold a shape: anything in constant rotation denies her the read, because she can only interpret a layout that holds still. Do not try to break the pair; the ceiling is not hers and cannot be removed without killing her, which is a worse outcome for her and a better one for you.
notes: The eighth gate is a routing limit, not a capacity limit. Modelling it as her realm ceiling is correct; modelling it as a weakness is not, because she has made a discipline of knowing it and will use that discipline.

The second channel is not a telepathy system and must not be given one. It reads qi layout, it is involuntary, and it is one remove from her own judgement, which is precisely why she cannot tell what she wants from what she is being routed towards.

The two-for-one liability is the setting's legal floor and should be honoured in any death, burial or save screen: this body produces two corpses and exactly one bill, and the record of that is the Grave of the Unnamed.

art.palette_notes: Wood-dark and ink with a jade undertone carried in the tendril tracery, warm ivory at collar and cuff, and cinnabar rationed entirely to the sternum root where the colony entered. The two halves must read as one garment rather than as two costumes, because the law that recognises her recognises one person. Ink contour slightly doubled along the forearms and throat where the tendril layer is visible under instrumentation.

identity.realm: the eleventh gate, never reached — her line ended at the third generation, well short of the wall

appearance.presentation: A small, spare, deeply still woman who reads objects before she looks at people. Gracile in a way the record confirms is real rather than an artefact, and carrying herself like a specimen she has grown used to being.
appearance.age: Thirty-four. Old for the third generation of her line and the only member of it alive.
appearance.build: Gracile and narrow, carrying less mass than a saltfolk, with long forearms and long hands, a shallow brine sac showing as a slight flatness across the upper back, and broad splayed feet.
appearance.complexion: Dry, pale and salt-crusted across the forearms and temples, with the dermal crust visible as a fine grey-white bloom on the shoulders that no amount of washing takes off.
appearance.hair: Bleached pale from the minerals, cropped flat at the back and kept extremely short, because a saltfolk's hair is the only part of them a pan wind can actually hurt.
appearance.eyes: Pale and faintly reddened at the inner corner from a lifetime of reading water in glare. The eyes are not her instrument; her tongue is.
appearance.palette: Pale mineral blue and warm ivory with a hard cinnabar line at the crust edge, and one warm note reserved throughout for whatever she is currently able to drink.
appearance.attire: A high-collared coat of undyed salt-stiffened canvas with long sleeves bound at the wrist and belted twice, over a close linen wrap. Sealed leather cuffs at both wrists. Boots soled for cracked pan and worn to nothing.
appearance.marks: Dermal salt crust over shoulders, forearms and jaw; flat splayed footprints pressed into the skin of the heels; and one old scar on the left forearm from a sump hatch.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely still and slightly turned, with the head angled as though reading the air. She positions herself so that a vessel, a wall or a person is always between her and any draught.

canon.role_in_story: The last member of a lineage that died of chemistry rather than of anything anybody did to it, kept viable by one sealed sump of the previous brine in a basin that no longer produces any. Her taste reads brine across four orders of dilution and reads the replacement perfectly well, which is the one measurement in the setting capable of showing that the basin's life law is running below its authored range — and the census that would have taken it was never run on her ground.
canon.first_appearance: First seen turning a beaker a hand's width before drinking from it, positioning the crust away from her mouth, in a sealed stone sump where nobody had thought to ask her what the water tasted like.
canon.lore: A Saltwrack is a saltfolk offshoot stranded on a basin whose brine was replaced rather than lost, so that everything the lineage was built to drink became poison to it and everything it could tolerate became nutritionally empty. They were never hunted, and there is nothing here of the ordinary kind of extinction: one element moved, and a species that had no alternative to that one element had nothing left. Their taste carries their senses and reads brine concentration across four orders of dilution — and it read the replacement brine perfectly well, which is the detail nobody involved found useful at the time. Nothing about the collapse left an anatomical trace, which is why it went unnoticed for two generations. Their three paths are all open and none was ever exercised at any scale, and they never reached the eleventh gate that every saltfolk stops at, because they ran out of generations first.
history: Born on a single evaporite basin whose brine never failed, into an offshoot gracile in a way every later specimen confirms was a real population difference and not an artefact of the remains.

Grew up reading brine concentration across four orders of dilution, which is what the species' taste carries, and finding the crust food and the water drinkable by every ordinary measure a person might apply.

Watched the basin change without the water being taken away. The brine was substituted rather than lost: what her body was built to drink became poison to it, and what it could tolerate had no nutrition in it at all.

Held for three declining generations. The last of them, her included, stayed viable only while the old brine persisted in one sealed sump — a single closed container of the previous chemistry in a basin that no longer had any of it.

Was never asked what she tasted. Her reading of the replacement brine was exact, the composition survey was never run on the basin, and by the time anybody with the right instrument thought to look at the water instead of at her, two generations had already gone.

personality.summary: Quiet, exact, and entirely un-used. She has spent a lifetime inside a sealed container on the strength of a faculty nobody ever thought to consult, and she carries no bitterness about it because she has nothing to compare it against — she has never once done the one thing she is good at for a purpose.
traits: reads any water without hesitation and has been asked about it perhaps a dozen times in her life
does not separate being helpful from being consulted, because the two have never come apart for her
enormously patient with the sealed sump and mildly impatient with everyone outside it
states what she tastes immediately and cannot understand why that is considered unusual
treats every question as the first half of a question she has never been given the second half of
mannerisms: tastes the air when she is thinking, which in her case is a measurement rather than a habit
turns any vessel a hand's width before drinking from it, putting the crust away from her mouth
asks what a thing is made of before she asks what it is for
sits with her back to a wall and her hands flat on her knees
holds still when a door opens and waits until the draught has passed
motivations: wants the composition survey run on her basin, two generations after it would have mattered
wants somebody to write down what the replacement brine actually is, in a document that outlives the sump
wants her line's third generation to have a shape somebody drew while it was still standing
wants to know whether the sump will outlast her, and has decided she would rather know
flaws: has never been trained in anything at all, including the one thing she is capable of
believes she is the last of her kind because nobody has told her otherwise and it has not occurred to her to check
has built an identity out of a faculty nobody wanted, which is the most dangerous thing available to her at her age
cannot survive fresh ground and has consequently never once had to become adaptable
personality.voice: Slow, plain and entirely without idiom. Answers the question she was asked, and then after a pause answers the one underneath it, because nobody has ever asked the second one and she has run out of things to say about the first. Repeats back exactly what she has been told before she offers anything of her own.
taboos: will not drink anything she has not read first
will not leave the sump for longer than the container may be left unattended
will not say that her kind is finished, having no evidence for it
will not permit a sample of the replacement brine to be called the old brine, even to be kind about it
will not answer a question about the past tense of her species without correcting it to the present

relationships.note: A dominion whose territory is exactly its waterline. Moving that line up the shore is the only way to give her ground and the only way to remove every subject who can drink where she would be, so she is kept rather than settled, and her survival costs less than an unanswered claim.

Their kidneys concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons, at the price of total dependence. Their taste carries the species across four orders of dilution, and hers reads the replacement brine perfectly well, which nobody involved found useful at the time.

The prize is the line itself and it cannot be split, because one of the two sides can only be helped by the other's removal. Her verdict would settle it, and settling it either way is the loss of one of the parties.

Counting seated groups against a tier's list is the method that produces an answer that does not change, and it was never run on this basin. The one instrument in the setting that could have shown a substituted brine as a life law running below its authored range went unused on the only body that needed it.

The Survey counts the groups a frame has actually seated rather than the groups it is permitted to seat. A substituted brine is precisely a life law running below its authored range, and this is the one method in the setting that would have shown it, and it is two generations too late for her basin.

The single biological answer to being trapped twice, metabolising brine and fresh water alike, and therefore a standing threat to the dominion's waterline and the only durable settlement either side has found. The crossing that would have saved her line happened, four generations ago, to somebody else's line.

No preparation, no site, no marker, and one line in a hand immediately destroyed. That is what happened anyway: a population that left no record at all, because the thing that was going to be written down was the chemistry of its own water.

reference_stats.summary: A gracile saltfolk body with a shallower brine sac and a mind path that is open and has never once been exercised at any scale. Her whole capability is perception: the species' taste reads brine concentration across four orders of dilution, and she reads the replacement brine exactly. She never came near the eleventh gate, because her line ended at the third generation of a famine.
strengths: reads the concentration of any brine across four orders of dilution, by taste, instantly and with no instrument at all
distinguishes the replacement water from the replacement brine with a certainty no measurement in the setting could match
sits indefinitely in a sealed hostile sump without deteriorating, because the chemistry in it is exactly right for her
entirely untrained, and therefore has no technique, no school and nothing whatsoever for an opponent to read
weaknesses: cannot drink fresh water at all and fails above the brine line inside about nine days
depends wholly on one sealed container of a chemistry the basin no longer produces
no cultivation practice on any of the three paths that are open to her
cannot fight, cannot travel and cannot be moved, and holds no reserve of any kind
is the most valuable person on a basin nobody has ever thought to measure
reference_stats.combat_read: She is not a combatant and the game should not pretend otherwise: no technique, no reserve, and no path trained to any scale. What she has instead is a reading far finer than anything else on the basin — she can tell a person what they have been drinking before they have finished swallowing it — which in a dispute whose verdict is a body measurement makes her simultaneously the most decisive and the least usable person on the ground. Do not put her in a fight. Put her in a room that contains water and let the answer arrive in front of people who are obliged to record it.
notes: Her mind path is open and has never been exercised at any scale. Model that as an untrained ceiling with no habits in it rather than as a low level, because those are very different things to fight.

The dominion's waterline is its only border, and her reading is the only measurement in the setting that could show the line is chemical rather than chosen. That is a story lever and must stay one rather than becoming a combat statistic.

The composition survey would have caught this and was never run on her basin. Any content chain about this basin should end with the survey being run far too late rather than with the truth being found in time.

art.palette_notes: Pale mineral blue and warm ivory with a hard cinnabar line at the crust edge, because her palette is a waterline and the whole character is a boundary. Desaturated almost to the point of dryness, with exactly one warm note reserved for whatever she is currently able to drink, and never for the sky. Ink contour fine, dry and unbroken — she has never worked in an environment that would have interrupted it.
